phases.title: Implement detection core: overlays, Louvain, cluster density

review_findings.message: Declared edges are keyed by base-node insertion indices but consumed as sorted-union positions: model::load interns nodes in table order (decisions, system_patterns, progress_entries, custom_data, code_nodes, then link endpoints), union_graph sorts the key universe (louvain.rs:113-125), yet base.edges are mapped by raw e.src/e.tgt (louvain.rs:132-134). Whenever insertion order differs from sort order -- any workspace containing custom_data or code_nodes rows, or link endpoints of a kind sorting before 'decision' -- every declared edge lands on the wrong node pair (trace: nodes [d1,d2,cd1] sort to [cd1,d1,d2], so edge (0,1) attaches cd1-d1 instead of d1-d2). Overlay pairs are translated through the NodeKey index (louvain.rs:157) and are unaffected. Existing tests pass only because their decision+progress_entry universes coincide. Fix: resolve e.src/e.tgt via base.nodes through the union index before keying pairs, and add a mixed-kind regression (decision+custom_data with a declared edge, asserting pair_strength lands on the right NodeKeys).
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: union_graph now translates both declared-edge endpoints through the NodeKey-to-union index (louvain.rs:137-146, the only raw-index consumption site); regression test declared_edges_attach_to_true_endpoints_when_orders_diverge (louvain.rs:636) builds an order-divergent universe and asserts true endpoint pairs carry the weights while raw-reuse pairs stay 0.0; test run and passed (15/15 louvain tests)

review_findings.message: Collapse self-loops are pushed twice: for a==b both super_adj[a].push((b,w)) and super_adj[b].push((a,w)) execute (louvain.rs:335-338), so a community's internal mass enters k, tot, comm_w[own], and m2 at 4*W_int instead of the 2*W_int the symmetric-replication convention yields. With a single push, super-level gains would be exactly 2x node-level gains (uniform doubling, sign-preserving), i.e. the textbook two-level objective; as written the objective is distorted -- internal cohesion is overweighted, making dense communities stickier and merge decisions biased relative to the spec's 'Louvain modularity optimization' (spec line 116). Still deterministic and monotone (it is a consistent delta-Q for a fixed, well-defined super-graph), so AC-2 holds. Fix: skip the second push when a==b.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: super_adj now pushes once for a==b behind an `if a != b` guard with an explanatory comment (louvain.rs:348-352), yielding the textbook two-level objective; 15/15 louvain tests pass including identical_clusters_on_repeated_db_runs

review_findings.message: Phase 2's recorded verification command 'cargo test schemas' matches zero tests anywhere in the repo (tests/schemas.rs is phase 3's suite; phase 2's tests are inline ops::graph::louvain::tests under the binary target). Verified: all targets report 0 passed with the filter, so this gate is vacuously green. Should read e.g. 'cargo test --bins louvain' (13 tests) until tests/schemas.rs exists.
review_findings.resolution: remaining: phase 2 verification still reads 'cargo test schemas' (progress.json:80) and the filter matches zero tests across all targets (verified: every target reports 0 passed); no test name containing 'schemas' exists yet and tests/schemas.rs is phase 3's suite. Claimed fix is not in the tree. Should read 'cargo test --bins louvain' (15 tests) until then

review_findings.message: Spec Architecture names the detection core src/ops/schemas/detect.rs (spec line 111); it landed as src/ops/graph/louvain.rs with no spec amendment and no deviation note in progress.json. Placement beside model.rs is defensible, but per the v12-correction precedent the spec text should be amended (or the module relocated) so the architecture section matches the shipped tree before phase 3 builds src/ops/schemas/ around it.
review_findings.resolution: remaining: no spec_deviations field exists in phase 2 and specs/0002-schema-formation.md is unamended (absent from the 6ec2eda diff); claimed recording is not in the tree. Spec Architecture still names src/ops/schemas/detect.rs

review_findings.message: co_retrieval groups grow the node universe with nodes absent from the base graph (union_graph extends keys from overlay groups, louvain.rs:113-118): retrieval_surfaces has no FK or uniqueness (schema.rs:205-211), so surfaces referencing deleted items persist as ghost nodes until phase 3 pruning, and a double-written event row double-counts a pair's ramp. The deliberate inclusion of overlay-only real items is correct and tested; the ghost-endpoint and double-write exposure should be an explicit decision (dedup per (ts,cmd,arg) group and/or skip unknown nodes) before phase 3 feeds real telemetry in.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: union_graph filters every overlay group member through base.contains(k) before extending the key universe (louvain.rs:113-123), so ghosts produce no node and no edges while real pairs still count the event; regression test surface_ghosts_do_not_extend_the_universe (louvain.rs:691) asserts decision-99 vanishes and pair strength equals 1.0 + co_weight(1); test run and passed

spec_deviations.reason: Detection is graph machinery; lives beside model.rs/code.rs/rel.rs under src/ops/graph/. src/ops/schemas/ remains the home for phase 3+ scan/apply/commands.

phases.title: Add staging, gates, and schema scan command

review_findings.message: AC-3's Then clause 'below-gate candidates appear as not-ready with the failed gate named' is unmet by the output contract: each candidate carries only a gates_pass boolean plus raw metrics (density, stability_count, reward_hits); no field names the failed gate, and the thresholds are private consts (DENSITY_GATE/STABILITY_GATE/REWARD_GATE), so a consumer cannot derive which gate failed from the JSON alone.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: scan output now carries per-gate gates objects {value, threshold, pass} plus a failed_gates name array (scan.rs:258-275), so AC-3's 'failed gate named' is met and thresholds are no longer private-only. Retry-2 caveat closed: failed_gates contents are pinned by sparse_cluster_stages_but_fails_density_gate (scan.rs:433 asserts ["density","stability"]) with gate value/threshold/pass pinned at scan.rs:434-441. Note: the CLI test asserts gates_pass only, not failed_gates; the JSON-shape pinning is unit-level.

review_findings.message: scan_writes_only_schema_candidates hardcodes an 11-table sample, not all tables: active_contexts, active_context_history, code_nodes, product_context, product_context_history, session_closes, and all four FTS tables are unchecked. code_nodes is in scan's own read path (model::load feeds the graph), so a regression mutating it would pass. Enumerate from sqlite_master (type='table', name != 'schema_candidates') for an exhaustive, rot-proof assertion.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: snapshot() (scan.rs:438-493) enumerates every table from sqlite_master, renders full row content for all storage classes (blob as hex), and falls back to natural order for WITHOUT ROWID FTS5 shadows; the audit compares before/after for all tables except schema_candidates, guarded by a presence assert. cargo test schemas: 7 passed.

review_findings.message: The Jaccard identity's edge paths are implemented but untested: assign()'s greedy tie-break (Jaccard desc, then cluster member set asc, then stored sig asc), the one-row-one-cluster constraint (second cluster matching a taken row must insert a fresh row), and upsert's drift-removed path all lack tests. A future assign() refactor could break determinism or winner selection and every existing test would stay green. The implementation itself is correct and deterministic on read.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: assign_prefers_higher_jaccard_order_independently (higher-J row wins in both stored orders), assign_is_one_to_one_when_two_clusters_match_one_row (exact-J cluster wins, loser stages fresh, both orders), and upsert_records_removed_drift_against_previous_members (drift-removed asserted against the persisted row: sig refreshed, drift 1/1, stability 2->3) cover the requested cases. Retry-2 residual closed: assign_tiebreaks_equal_jaccard_distinct_clusters_by_member_set (scan.rs:608-626) constructs genuinely J-equal distinct sets (both 5/6 vs the row, verified by intersection/union math) and asserts the lexicographically smaller member set wins in both caller orders; comparator level 2 is clusters[a].cmp(&clusters[b]) (scan.rs:145), matching the test. cargo test schemas: 9 passed.

review_findings.message: No CLI-level test invokes 'engrams schema scan' — all 4 tests call scan(&conn) directly, so arg parsing, dispatch wiring (Command::Schema -> schemas::handle), and JSON serialization of the command output are unexercised; tests/cli.rs precedent covers every other command family at the binary level.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: test_schema_scan_stages_and_writes_nothing_else (tests/cli.rs:2176) drives the real binary (assert_cmd, stdout parsed as JSON), seeds a dense triangle via CLI + SQL fixture, asserts one candidate, stability 1->2->3 with gates_pass flipping only on the third sighting, stable cluster_sig across scans, and a write audit asserting zero row deltas outside schema_candidates. Quality notes: the CLI-level write audit is a 4-table delta count (schema_candidates/decisions/context_links/item_anchors), not the exhaustive snapshot - exhaustiveness remains in the unit-level scan_writes_only_schema_candidates; and the gates flip is asserted from gates_pass, not the failed_gates array (unit-level failed_gates pinning covers the shape). Fixture seeding anchors by SQL with a documented reason (anchor add would materialize code nodes and join a fourth member). Test run and passed.

review_findings.message: Staging upserts run outside a transaction: a mid-scan failure leaves earlier rows advanced and later rows not, and the next scan advances the advanced rows again, inflating their stability_count by one sighting. Repo precedent (import.rs) wraps multi-row writes in a transaction; one unchecked_transaction around the upsert loop fixes it.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: one unchecked_transaction wraps the whole upsert loop with commit after (scan.rs:231-279); any upsert error propagates via ? and drops the tx, rolling back all staged rows.

review_findings.message: spec_deviations is null for phase 3: the orchestrator-approved removal of UnionGraph.index (HashMap lookup replaced by binary search over the sorted nodes slice, tests migrated to a gpos helper) is a structural deviation from the phase-2-era detection design and must be recorded here with status approved-by-orchestrator, as was done for the detect.rs path deviation in phase 2.
review_findings.resolution: remaining: spec_deviations still null for phase 3 after retry 2 (re-verified via jq); the approved UnionGraph.index removal remains unrecorded. Not claimed fixed by the implementer this retry.

review_findings.message: Retry 1 introduced clippy noise where the phase was previously clean: unused 'use std::fmt::Write as _;' in production scope (scan.rs:14, the only write! call lives in the test module, which gets the trait via use super::*), and three clippy::cloned_ref_to_slice_refs suggestions in the new tests (scan.rs:540, 541, 554). cargo clippy --all-targets now reports 1 warning on the bin and 3 on the test build.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: cargo clippy --all-targets reports 0 warnings after retry 2 (re-run this re-review; was 1 bin + 3 test warnings).
